state.prepare:
Workspace preparation before start (mandatory decision table; the skill has the full version):
1) Dirty workspace -> ask the user: [stop | auto commit (AI-generated message)]; free text from the user directs you instead — never lose uncommitted work.
2) Clean + on main/master -> no question: name the feature branch yourself (e.g. sfd/<slug>) and create it from main.
3) Clean + off main -> compute ahead/behind vs main, then offer the user exactly these options (always plus "stop"): 0/0 -> [stay | new branch from current]; ahead>0,behind=0 -> [stay | new from current | new from main (switch to main first) | fast-forward main to current, then stay]; ahead=0,behind>0 -> [stay | new from current | new from main (switch to main first) | fast-forward to main, then branch from it]; ahead>0,behind>0 (diverged) -> [stay | new from current | new from main (switch to main first) | you merge with main, resolve all conflicts, and continue].
4) No main-like ref / detached HEAD / merge in progress -> ask the user how to proceed (always include "stop"); never guess a base.
Branch naming, creation, duplicate handling and any merge are your own git operations.
state.handoff: You now drive the start: first read the sectioned-feature-development skill, then determine the task to build. If this conversation has no task context yet, ask the user what they want before doing anything else. Once the task is known, perform workspace preparation per the decision table above and create the feature branch, then call the sfd_start tool with a one-line taskSummary (optional slug, branch) — it performs no git operations; it records the git facts it observes and persists the initial state.
state.nextPlan: Next: read the sectioned-feature-development skill, identify Feature(s) from the user request, and draft PLAN-FULL at .agent-work/PLAN-FULL.md. Automatic activation requires user approval of the first proportional plan before plan review.
